solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: State agent caught you — beginning of life in pen

indicators.note: 'in' puts the letter inside the word that follows, as a thing is held in a pen

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, is an agent
a Bic is a ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: A secret agent catches someone red-handed and a life sentence in the pen follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' reads as prison in the surface, but it is the brand of ballpoint. 'Caught' only joins the agent to you.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the political sense: a republic is a nation, a state without a monarch.

clue.text: Carbuncle I noticed when chatting

indicators.note: chatting is speech, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: to notice is to see, so 'I noticed' = I saw

explanation.surface: Someone mentions in conversation that they spotted a boil.
explanation.walkthrough: Said without the final R, as in most British speech, I SAW sounds just like the answer. Carbuncle recalls Prince Charles's 'monstrous carbuncle' jibe at a building design.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: a carbuncle is a boil, and by extension an ugly building that spoils the view.

clue.text: Without trial incarcerating prisoner — no questions asked?

indicators.note: to incarcerate is to lock up inside, so the prisoner goes inside

explanation.surface: Someone jailed without a trial and nobody asked why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without trial' looks like legal injustice but simply means not tried out, and the prisoner is locked inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: when no questions are asked, nothing is disputed; the question mark flags the loose paraphrase.

clue.text: Look to take advantage of miserable individual

parts.note: to use someone is to take advantage of them

explanation.surface: A warning to watch out for a wretch who exploits people.
explanation.walkthrough: LO is the old exclamation of 'lo and behold', a crossword staple for look.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: louse, like rat or worm, is slang for a contemptible person.

clue.text: Cash for one slicing tea bread

indicators.note: 'for one' marks Cash as one example of a person, so we want his first name
a knife slicing a loaf goes into it, so the name goes into the middle of the tea

explanation.surface: Money handed over by a person cutting a loaf at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cash' looks like money, but it is the Australian tennis player. 'Tea bread' reads as one thing; tea is wordplay and bread the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: bread covers the unleavened Indian flatbread cooked on a griddle.

clue.text: Deft chopper eliminating American

indicators.note: to eliminate is to get rid of, so the A is thrown out of the chopper

parts.note: a cleaver is a butcher's chopper

explanation.surface: A skilful axeman who gets rid of an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' may suggest a helicopter; it is a kitchen blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone skilful and quick with their hands or mind.

clue.text: Cries, deleting one chapter, done with rewriting climax

indicators.note: rewriting a word sets its letters down again in a new order
to delete is to strike out, so the one is struck out of CRIES

explanation.surface: An author cuts a tearful chapter and, having finished a rewrite, reaches the climax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deleting one chapter' looks like one instruction, but only the one is deleted; chapter then adds its own letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose musical sense: strictly a crescendo is the build-up, but it is widely used for the peak itself.

clue.text: Jacob's mother possibly lives in Tunbridge Wells

indicators.note: to live in a place is to be found inside it, so the answer is found inside these words

explanation.surface: A query about whether Jacob's mother has a house in a genteel Kent town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible makes you think of Rebekah, but the Jacob here is a sheep. Tunbridge Wells is a Kent spa town known for prim letter-writers.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a Jacob is a breed of piebald sheep, so its mother is a ewe; 'possibly' marks the example.

clue.text: Name read back — misspelt it nevertheless — missing some letters

indicators.note: to read back is to read in the reverse direction, right to left
the words lose letters at each end, leaving only an inner run

explanation.surface: A complaint that a name, read aloud from a document, was misspelt with letters left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misspelt' tempts you to rearrange letters, but it only supplies the start of the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to entitle a book or a person is to give it a title, a name.

clue.text: Support in French monarch's household protects mature people

indicators.note: to protect is to wrap round and shield, so the court surrounds the rest

explanation.surface: A French king's retinue guarding its elders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French monarch' seems to belong together, but French goes with 'in'. 'Mature' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: support in the sense of cheering someone on, not holding them up.

clue.text: Black cat energy

parts.note: the ounce is the snow leopard

explanation.surface: A black cat full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The ounce is an old name for the snow leopard, a big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: bounce is the springy vigour of a lively person, their energy.

clue.text: True account by cleric

parts.note: a curate is an assistant priest

explanation.surface: A vicar's testimony that is trustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: AC is the standard abbreviation for account, as on bank statements.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a true figure and an accurate one are both correct.

clue.text: Engineers instinctive about vehicle revived with new body

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the instinctive word goes round the vehicle

explanation.surface: Mechanics with a feel for cars restore one and give it new bodywork.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a car restoration, with 'body' as bodywork; the definition is a soul reborn.
explanation.definitionFit: The literal sense: to reincarnate is to bring a soul back to life in another body.

clue.text: When drunk, never share, lacking resistance and respect

indicators.note: to lack is to be without, so the share goes without its R
a drunk staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice that a drunk should never split the round, and should drop their respect.
explanation.walkthrough: R = resistance, from physics formulae.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: veneration is respect raised to reverence.

clue.text: Sailor read aloud, not enjoying the first time, gave up

indicators.note: to enjoy can mean to have, so not enjoying is not having

parts.note: to dictate is to read out for someone to write
t = time; the first T of DICTATED goes

explanation.surface: A sailor, reading something out and not liking it the first time, quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read aloud' is not asking for a sound-alike; it means spoken for someone to write down. Only the first of its two Ts is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialised sense: abdicating is giving up a throne or duty, the formal word for gave up.

clue.text: 100 trapped in mine maybe frozen

indicators.note: what is trapped in something is held inside it, so the 100 sits inside the mine

parts.note: an IED, improvised explosive device, such as a mine

explanation.surface: A hundred miners trapped underground, perhaps frozen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' reads as a pit, but it is the explosive kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: iced water and frozen water are the same thing, turned solid by cold.

clue.text: Join a returning vessel

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the letters run the other way

explanation.surface: An instruction to board a ship coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' looks like a ship; it is a container for liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: two properties that abut join along a shared edge.

clue.text: Bans volunteers no longer welcoming one member of serving staff

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the bans take the one inside

parts.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve of volunteer soldiers, now renamed the Army Reserve

explanation.surface: A cafe stops taking volunteers but takes on one paid server.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' is not a deletion: it says the volunteers' name is a former one.
explanation.definitionFit: A modern sense: a barista is the person behind a coffee bar, one of the serving staff.

clue.text: Upset record previously charted at fourth and fifth positions only

indicators.text: at fourth and fifth positions only
indicators.note: positions are places in the word, so only the letters in places four and five are kept

explanation.surface: A record that once charted, only reaching number four or five, causing an upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The chart-positions surface makes you think of the Top 40, but the positions are letter positions in 'charted'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to upset someone and to disconcert them both mean to fluster.

clue.text: Four of them are on the fiddle!

definitions.text: Four of them are on the fiddle!

parts.note: reads as four crooks, but counts parts of an instrument
'on the fiddle' is British slang for cheating; here the fiddle is a violin

explanation.surface: Four people running a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the fiddle' means cheating, but read literally it puts things on a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: a violin carries four strings, the instrument's own parts rather than people.

clue.text: Full development of much of Peterlee

indicators.note: developing something changes its form, so the letters are reshaped
much of a thing is most but not all of it, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: The complete build-out of a town.
explanation.walkthrough: Peterlee is a post-war new town in County Durham, so 'development' fits the surface as town planning.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: replete means filled to capacity, full, especially after food.

clue.text: Expert meeting crude dancing farmer?

indicators.note: dancers move about, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A pro meets a farmer doing a vulgar dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the farmer as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a farmer is a food producer, the question mark signalling the example.

clue.text: Band beginning to sound rubbish

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pop group that starts off sounding terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' is a group of musicians in the surface, but here it is a strip of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the visual sense: a stripe is a band of colour.

clue.text: Dash into store on vacation for waders

indicators.note: to go into a place is to enter it, so the dash enters the store
a place on vacation is vacated, emptied, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: to nip is to dash quickly

explanation.surface: Running into a shop on holiday to buy fishing boots.
explanation.walkthrough: Waders sound like boots for anglers, but they are wading birds; the answer is its own plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: snipe are long-billed marsh birds, among the waders.

clue.text: Aging tips, time to change — it looks no different!

definitions.note: the definition is a clause describing the noun phrase

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so the letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: Beauty advice for ageing, with a promise that nothing will look different.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the answer rather than naming it: something that looks no different from the original.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom described rather than named: the phrase means an exact likeness of someone.

clue.text: Fish leaving hint it might have been kept in well?

definitions.text: it might have been kept in well?

indicators.note: to leave is to depart, so the fish departs from the hint

explanation.surface: A fish swims off, perhaps having once lived in a well.
explanation.walkthrough: The well is the kind on an old school desk, not a water well.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: writing fluid was kept in the inkwell of old desks, so the well is not a water well.

clue.text: Got hot soaking up bit of sun?

definitions.text: Got hot soaking up bit of sun?

indicators.note: to soak up is to absorb, so the word for got hot takes the letter inside
a bit of a word is a small part of it, here its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone warming up by taking in the sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and a description of lying in the sun, the question mark allowing that this is not always getting hot.
explanation.definitionFit: An &lit: the whole clue reads straight as lying in the sun's warmth and heating up.

clue.text: Biased eastern revolutionary driven through with spike

explanation.surface: A slanted report of an Eastern rebel being impaled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' often signals reversal, but here it is a noun, a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: The literal sense: pierced through, as meat is on a kebab stick.
